blocks.x: -- you liked about Louie, it was always going to be different, or it was always --
He always played around the melody, even his solos, you can still hear the melody.
Oh, yeah. Right.
What used to knock me out the most about Louie, when he played a verse to a tune. I liked the way he played that verse.
Yeah, I remember the record "Squeeze Me," he played a verse, just guitar. Awfully pretty.

Because he liked -- you know, he'd play stock arrangements. He used to do that, we'd always play the verse, introduction then the verse, and he'd take the lead on the verse. Very good first trumpet man.
Uh-huh.
Yeah, they'd just swing in. That swinging lead, oh, that killed me.
That sound, too. Beautiful sound that he --
You know, Nappy kind of played a little bit like Louie, too, you know.
Yeah. Yeah, I like the way Nappy plays. Nappy's got a lot of lung power in his playing.
The air. Lot of power.
And you never know what's going to happen. Never knew!
One of my favorite trumpet players, though, was always Bobby Ballard.
Oh, my goodness.
Plays so sweet.
Don't mention Bob Ballard. Oh, he was the sweetest trumpet player I know of.
Just beautiful. And Norm Murphy, too.
Yeah, Norm Murphy.
Norm's straight.
When he's straight, boy, he can play.
Lot of good musicians.
